title: RouteLLM-style shadow route calibration on real run telemetry (offline, advice only)
summary: The supervisor ran `agent.py orchestrate route-calibration` over the real local orchestrator home: 26 runs, 386 editing nodes (354 labeled, 32 unlabeled; 401 reviewer nodes excluded), 0 malformed lines. Shadow mode; routing was not changed. Advice: escalate earlier for implementer, repairer and test_author nodes on the fast and balanced classes (planner: insufficient data). Across thresholds the curve is flat (cheap share 0.4802, kept pass rate 0.8824, 45 escalations avoided), so the deciding signal is per-cell failure rate, not a threshold. This matches what was observed on 2026-10-02: fast-tier (Haiku) implementers repeatedly exhausted five review rounds and needed gate approval with findings still open. Recommended next step: a bounded experiment that starts implementer/test_author nodes one class higher (fast to balanced) and compares review rounds and cost per accepted node, before any routing change.
